topic: A technically valid AI-made video that failed human review
thesis: Machine QA can verify delivery properties, but human taste and trust remain release criteria.

sources.notes: Primary local evidence: src/content/shorts/codex-research-first-en/codex-research-first-en.mp4 (SHA-256 dffda12d3f90e2432c0d451cf2df0574bd2f571b0fcce54387c0b573bccc734c), its QA report (SHA-256 768d3183bfa6a5d2ef05443a5b2f17a025f6051779aada85f86cd0ce3c53fba3), and the approved pilot treatment. The repository URL identifies the owning project; the exact local paths and hashes are the verification record.
Direction reference only. No frames or audio from this post are reused in the pilot.
Current model-specific terms cover Music v1 and v2. The applicable plan must permit the intended media use; generation through the paid API is recorded in the music manifest.

facts.claim: The source video is 1920×1080 at 60 fps, its encoded mix measured about -16.2 LUFS, and a full decode test completed without errors.
facts.sensitivity: These measurements describe this exact encoded file, not creative quality.

facts.claim: Aaron's immediate feedback was that the music was bad and the recreated demo visibly looked fake.
facts.sensitivity: The English on-screen lines are approved translations of Chinese feedback, not verbatim English quotations.

facts.claim: Technical delivery checks do not measure taste or viewer trust, so this workflow now treats human review as a release gate.
facts.sensitivity: This is Aaron Studio's operating rule, not a universal empirical claim.
